authority_split.downstream_verification_must_not_be_conf: the Python harness re-derives transaction ids, Merkle roots and canonical serializations from the published hex as a second opinion about the *encoding*, and a C++ port will later be diffed against the *verdicts* in P4.2B (P4.2B, not this milestone). Neither one generates an expected value here, and neither one has been run against a C++ Block Structure validator, because this milestone does not implement one and claims no parity with it.
authority_split.exporter_declaration_check: each fixture carries a declared construction intent — the design contract's predicted variant, payload and rule set — which `p42_emit` compares with what the reference returned and panics on if they differ. The declarations are inputs to the export, not fields of the corpus, so no predicted value can reach a published file.
rust_is_the_only_origin_of: leaf ids and serialized transaction bytes

instead_guaranteed_by: `.iso_08_no_transactions` and `.pair_07_08_bits_and_empty`: B-8 is reached without any read of `transactions[0]`, so an empty list cannot be masked by a later rule
`.iso_09_too_many_transactions`: `count == 2001` returns `TooManyTransactions` with the length read back out of the variant
`.pair_09_10_over_limit_and_first_not_coinbase`: B-9 dominates B-10, and the list carries no coinbase at all, so the verdict cannot be attributed to the coinbase scan
the emitter's per-case assertion that the derived violated set never holds both 8 and 9
deferred_pairs.not_claimed: this corpus does not claim to have experimentally proven which of B-8 and B-9 a conforming port checks first, and no `.pair_08_09` case identifier exists.
deferred_pairs.reason: `transactions.is_empty()` and `transactions.len() > MAX_BLOCK_TRANSACTIONS` are mutually exclusive, so no input can violate both rows at once and no input can distinguish the two relative orders. The relative order of B-8 and B-9 is observationally vacuous.

deferred_pairs.not_claimed: nothing here asserts B-13 precedes B-14, in either direction.
deferred_pairs.reason: the pair is representable — a far-future timestamp together with a stale root — but the corrected P4.2 design contract did not freeze a case for it, and this milestone does not add one. A port's ordering of these two rows is therefore not covered by this corpus yet.

description: Rust-authoritative validation fixtures for the Block Structure rules B-3 through B-15 of `zerocoin::consensus::block::Block::validate_structure`, generated for the C++ kernel's future port of that function. This is a fixture-first milestone: it publishes what Rust returns, and it does not implement, run or claim agreement from any C++ validator.
determinism: no wall clock, RNG, wallet, data directory or network is used: `now` is a literal in every case, including the three that put it next to `u64::MAX` to separate saturating from wrapping addition

every header nonce comes from `consensus::pow::mine`, a deterministic single-thread upward scan from zero, or from the same deterministic failing-nonce scan `consensus_rules.rs` uses; neither depends on a thread count or a clock

every transaction is a literal: `coinbase_transaction` at a fixed height with the published key 1, one of the P0 fixture shapes from a single seed byte, or one of the two filler shapes with the index carried in `lock_time` so no two leaves collide
the 2000 and 2001 cases are the same list at two lengths, so the accepted/rejected pair differs by one transaction and one root
five cases are rebuilt from the committed P4.1 corpus on disk, and the rebuild is compared with the published bytes before anything is derived from them
JSON object keys are emitted in sorted order by serde_json
generator: zerocoin/tests/export_baseline_vectors.rs, `p42_*` functions, added by the P4.2A commit that lands immediately after the baseline; no fixture can record the hash of the commit that contains it, and none here claims to have existed before this exporter did
independent_verifier: test/harness/zro_vectors.py already provides the transaction deserializer, `tx_txid`, `tx_is_coinbase` and `merkle_root` needed to re-derive every published digest and every `serialized_hex` from bytes alone; `run_vectors.py` registers no verifier for this group and this corpus does not wire one in, so the Rust exporter remains the origin of every value published here
notes: `MAX_BLOCK_TRANSACTIONS` is 2000 and the guard is `len() > 2000`, so 2000 is admitted and 2001 is rejected with the length published back out of the variant.

`validate_structure` is called directly, with the seven arguments the reference's own in-source test uses, and never through `Chain::connect_block`: the large-list transactions spend UTXOs that do not exist, and `connect_block` additionally runs `difficulty::validate_bits` and the reward and UTXO checks that a structural fixture has no business asserting.

Three orderings are deliberately not conflated here: `error_kind` names the `BlockError` variant, `reported_rule` is the row of `validate_structure`'s body that returned it, and the kernel's own `BlockErrorKind` numbering is a C++-side sequence this corpus does not assign or assert.
B-15 is reachable only when B-14 passed, which is why `.iso_15_insufficient_pow` claims its own root — a shape the P4.1 corpus cannot contain at all.
The version field is published and never validated (F-2), so no case here depends on it; `BLOCK_VERSION` is written by `header_at` and read by nothing in the path under test.

These 34 cases are new with the `p42_*` exporter. `reference_commits` names the commit whose code is under test, not the commit that introduced these cases, because a fixture cannot truthfully claim to predate its own generator.

precedence.basis: a pair is represented when one case's published input violates both rows and `reported_rule` equals the smaller of them. The emitter asserts that equality for all 34 cases, so the array above is a summary of assertions that ran during generation, not a list of hopes.

provenance: b71d769be8357bcf10d768d915770125cf7f7c24 — see `source_commit_rule`, `generator` and `reference_commits`; the origin of every expected value is the Rust function named in `description`, called directly by the exporter
regenerate: ZRO_VECTOR_WRITE=1 with the same command, then review the diff
reuse_meaning: the listed cases replay a committed `chain.claimed_merkle_root` block byte for byte — the same header fields, the same serialized transactions, the same seven-key validation context — and add only a validator-level claim P4.1 could not make. `p42_reference_fixtures_are_reproducible_and_pinned` compares them against `test/p41-vectors/chain/claimed_merkle_root.json` on disk, so the identity is checked against the published corpus rather than against a second copy of the same emitter call. The P4.1 corpus itself is not modified by this milestone.

rule_coverage.note: `reported_by_at_least_one_case` is the set of guards some case had the reference actually name; `violated_in_at_least_one_case` is the set of guards some case's published input fails, whether or not an earlier one masked it. Both are computed from the cases at export, so neither is a claim this file makes on its own behalf.

source_commit_rule: the newest commit that touches a Rust build input (`zerocoin/src`, `zerocoin/Cargo.toml`, `zerocoin/Cargo.lock`, `zerocoin/build.rs`) and therefore the production code that produced every value here; `zerocoin/src` is byte-identical between it and the baseline this corpus is committed on. Between it and `reference_commits.validate_structure_introduced` the only edit to `block.rs` extracts B-3 and B-4 into `validate_header_identity`, which changes the call graph and no verdict.
synthetic_context_meaning: a case labelled synthetic deliberately combines published values that a running node would never produce together — `median_time_past` above `now + MAX_FUTURE_SECONDS`, or eleven guards broken in one block. The isolation and boundary cases reach their verdicts with ordinary contexts; these two need the label so no reader mistakes an observation about guard order for an observation about the network.
